result.title: From Perception to Simulation: Unveiling and Empowering Mental Spatial Dynamics in MLLMs
result.summary: Spatial reasoning is a fundamental component of world understanding for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). While existing research has advanced the perception of spatial relations in static scenes, the domain of dynamic spatial simulation remains relatively unexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce MentalGrid, a benchmark focused on spatial reasoning tasks that require models to simulate evolving spatial states without intermediate visual feedback. Extensive evaluation on our benchmark reveals a significant deficiency in the spatial simulation capabilities of existing models. Specifically, we find that performance is constrained by perceptual limitations in simple simulation scenarios and hindered by inadequate multi-step reasoning as complexity increases. To address these challenges, we propose a three-stage curriculum learning framework utilizing 16k specialized spatial reasoning samples. This approach yields SpatialWalker, which achieves a 33.8% average improvement over its base model, surpassing proprietary models like Gemini-3-Flash in spatial simulation. Furthermore, SpatialWalker demonstrates robust generalization, maintaining a 4.9% average gain on out-of-domain benchmarks, demonstrating the pivotal role of spatial simulation as a fundamental building block for broader spatial intelligence.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MentalGrid 基准，考察 MLLM 在无中间视觉反馈条件下模拟空间状态演化的能力，并指出简单场景受感知限制、复杂场景受多步推理不足限制，进而用 1.6 万条空间样本的三阶段课程学习训练出 SpatialWalker。
AI.relevance_reason: 「无中间视觉反馈的动态空间状态模拟」直接涉及 VLM 内部状态是否保留任务必要几何信息及多步状态更新，其感知／推理瓶颈分解与课程训练可供核查内部状态使用与视觉旁路的区分。
